ukmt-jmo-2023-a01.title: Mixed number
ukmt-jmo-2023-a01.body:
$59\div13=4$ remainder $7$, so $\frac{59}{13}=4\frac7{13}$, which is more than $4\frac12$. Nearest integer: $5$.

**Answer: 5**

ukmt-jmo-2023-a03.title: Exterior angles
ukmt-jmo-2023-a03.body:
The marked angles are vertically opposite to the four exterior angles of the central quadrilateral, which sum to $360^\circ$. So the marked angles sum to $2\times360^\circ=720^\circ$.

**Answer: 720 degrees**

ukmt-jmo-2023-a05.title: Distances
ukmt-jmo-2023-a05.body:
Total length $110$. Distance from $-55$ to $5.5$ is $60.5$. $\frac{60.5}{110}=0.55$.

**Answer: 55%**

ukmt-jmo-2023-a07.title: Count faces
ukmt-jmo-2023-a07.body:
Joined, the top and bottom each show an L-shape of area $7$ cm$^2$, there are four square faces of area $4$ and four rectangular faces of area $2$. Total $2\times7+4\times4+4\times2=38$.

**Answer: 38 cm$^2$**

ukmt-jmo-2023-a08.title: Sums
ukmt-jmo-2023-a08.body:
Total of all six: $12126$. Alex's three sum to $3\times2023=6069$. Others: $12126-6069=6057$, mean $2019$.

**Answer: 2019**

ukmt-jmo-2023-a09.title: Heights
ukmt-jmo-2023-a09.body:
Side $5$; rhombus height $20\div5=4$. So the horizontal offset of $U$ from $Q$ is $\sqrt{25-16}=3$. The unshaded part of the square under $UT$ is a trapezium with parallel sides $2$ and $5$ and height $4$: area $14$. Shaded $=25-14=11$.

**Answer: 11 cm$^2$**

ukmt-jmo-2023-a10.title: Last digits
ukmt-jmo-2023-a10.body:
$10^5=2^5\cdot5^5$ is a multiple of $32$, so only the last five digits matter: $32323=32\times1010+3$. Remainder $3$.

**Answer: 3**

ukmt-jmo-2023-b01.title: Inequality
ukmt-jmo-2023-b01.body:
$\frac12+\frac13+\frac1{10}=\frac{28}{30}=\frac{14}{15}$. We need $\frac1n<\frac1{15}$, i.e. $n>15$. So $n$ can be any integer greater than $15$.

**Answer: $n\ge16$**

ukmt-jmo-2023-b02.title: Pick units
ukmt-jmo-2023-b02.body:
Let total distance be $10x$ and total time $5t$. First part: distance $x$ in time $t$, speed $\frac xt$. Rest: $9x$ in $4t$, speed $\frac{9x}{4t}$. Ratio $1:\frac94=4:9$.

**Answer: 4 : 9**

ukmt-jmo-2023-b03.title: Algebra
ukmt-jmo-2023-b03.body:
Let there be $n$ initially. After five stops: $n-5+5x=nx$, so $n(x-1)=5(x-1)$. As $x\neq1$, $n=5$.

**Answer: 5**

ukmt-jmo-2023-b04.title: Angle chase
ukmt-jmo-2023-b04.body:
Interior angles: nonagon $140^\circ$, hexagon $120^\circ$. Hexagon $HIABCD$ has angle sum $720^\circ$ and by symmetry $\angle DHI=\angle CDH$, so $\angle DHI=\frac{720-4\cdot140}{2}=80^\circ$.

In triangle $HIM$: $\angle HIM=140-120=20^\circ$ and $HI=MI$ (equal sides of the regular polygons), so $\angle MHI=\frac{180-20}2=80^\circ$. As $\angle MHI=\angle DHI$ (with $M$, $D$ on the same side of $HI$), $H,M,D$ are collinear. ∎

ukmt-jmo-2023-b05.title: Eliminate
ukmt-jmo-2023-b05.body:
The number is divisible by at least two of $2,4,8$, so by $4$ (in fact $2$ and $4$ both hold); hence $B
e5$ and, since $90$ is not divisible by $4$, $B
eq0$. So $5
mid N$ and $N$ is divisible by all of $1,2,3,4,6,7,8,9$. Divisibility by $8$: last three digits $89B$ must be a multiple of $8$; only $896$, so $B=6$. Divisibility by $9$: digit sum $A+51$ divisible by $9$, so $A=3$. (One checks $31234567896=7	imes4462081128$.)

**Answer: $A=3$, $B=6$**

ukmt-jmo-2023-b06.title: Square then the fifth
ukmt-jmo-2023-b06.body:
Corners $A,B,C,D$ form a 4-cycle. If $B,D$ have the same colour: $3\cdot2\cdot2=12$ ways. If different: $6$ ways for $B,D$ and then $A,C$ are forced: $6$. Total $18$. The fifth circle is joined to one corner so has $2$ choices: $18\times2=36$.

**Answer: 36**
